_preregistration.definition: structural = fraction of newline/markup/digit chars in the first 200 >= 0.15 (p95 of the Pile; p1 scores 0.230, p97.6). prose control <= 0.02. Rows taken in INDEX ORDER after thresholding, never read for content.
_preregistration.rung: t0 IS F154's p1 and must reproduce it exactly
_preregistration.primary: up-rate under structural vs prose text, on the three models F154 showed raisable
_preregistration.control_check: the unraisable model must stay unraisable, or F154's model-property claim is wrong
_preregistration.not_a_test: three raisable clusters cannot fail a significance test informatively; rates only, no p-value
_preregistration.why: p1 is one text, and a hypothesis read off one observation is the defect this project keeps catching -- F153's 'all up-texts are Shakespeare' died the same way

verdict: RUNG (t0 is F154's p1 and must reproduce it): 8 cells, worst error 0.00e+00. Identical. ANTI-VACUITY: 0 model(s) lack room to move both ways, so all can show either direction. PRIMARY, up-rate under STRUCTURAL vs PROSE text, on the models F154 showed are raisable: Falcon3-1B-Base struct 4/6 vs prose 1/6; Minerva-3B-base-v1.0 struct 3/6 vs prose 1/6; Qwen1.5-1.8B struct 0/6 vs prose 1/6. Totals: structural 7/18, prose 3/18.  CONSISTENCY: 2 of 3 raisable models individually show a HIGHER up-rate under structural than under prose (['Falcon3-1B-Base', 'Minerva-3B-base-v1.0']); 1 do not (['Qwen1.5-1.8B']). The models DISAGREE, so the pooled rate is NOT read as a summary -- pooling across units that point different ways is the Simpson's shape this project was already caught by (F141), and the per-model split below is the result instead.  VERDICT: PARTIAL and model-dependent. Structural text raises 2 of 3 raisable models more often than prose does, and REVERSES or fails on the rest. The pooled ratio (7/18 vs 3/18) clears the pre-registered bar, but it is carried by a subset, so the honest claim is that the MECHANISM IS ITSELF MODEL-DEPENDENT -- which is what every other finding in this programme also says. It does NOT yield a predictive rule about prefixes. CONTROL, the model F154 found unraisable (0/12 up): SmolLM-1.7B struct 1/6 vs prose 0/6. STRUCTURAL TEXT RAISES IT. F154's claim that bidirectionality is a fixed model property is WRONG -- the model was only unraisable by the texts tried, and that finding needs revising. NOT A TEST, declared before the numbers: 3 raisable model clusters cannot fail a significance test informatively, so this estimates RATES and no p-value is computed. BOUNDARY: 4 models, 6 structural and 6 prose texts from ONE corpus at ONE length (9 tokens), under ONE operationalisation of 'structural' (newline/markup/digit density >= 0.15 over the first 200 chars, vs <= 0.02). Rows were chosen by INDEX ORDER after thresholding, never by reading them.
